Brief 011 C · round 4 · 28 HUD variations

Sky: "still not happy with the HUD, show me lots of variations." A wide exploration, not a refinement of d3: footprints from nothing docked to a Syndicate column, seven visual languages, six ways to give orders, seven icon treatments, five price displays. Same beat first (0:58, Pay on Inez), then the six strongest live.

All 28 on the real café plate at 1920x1080, grouped by footprint (how much is docked, from nothing to a Syndicate column). Not broken by any: price shown before commit on every order (the "pay" cut-downs below are the exception, listed), outcome "?" until the temperament is known, signals only as small pictograms, every UI colour >= 21.3 from the three signals. Not shown in any beat: the investigator question-mark icon and its dotted line of leads (no investigator is in these three moments); it carries over unchanged from round 3.

7 · Glyph's top five, and why

  1. v10 Signage hotbar. Keeps every rule (full price, "?" outcomes), the roster is the Syndicate idea at 1.5 % of the screen, the keys make it feel like a live game, and the street stays clean. Cost: Q/W/E/R verb keys replace E/F/C in §10.
  2. v01 Light in the road. The one that stops looking like a HUD: rings of light in the pavement, a floating orb for the verb, the price as four arcs on the ground. 0.04 % docked; this is the world's own motif. Risk: the arcs are the hardest thing here to read at 1080p, and the clock rides the agent.
  3. v06 Slim enamel, small radial. The safe answer if the enamel is not the problem: d3 on a diet (about 1.3 % of the screen instead of d3's ~12 %), every rule intact, no control changes.
  4. v23 Syndicate, literal. Honest benchmark of what "literal" costs: a 5 % column, readable portraits, verbs on each slot. The pixel face sells the reference at once, but it sits oddly on the smooth 3D street. Right-click default is a control change.
  5. v04 Fan of four (monoline). Nothing docked, verbs fan off the agent that will do the job, a halo arc carries the number. The lightest touch on the street. Needs the 50 s restored to its capsule to keep the rule.

Reading across all 28: the footprint measure supports the guess that d3 was heavy (about 12 % of the frame at the pick moment; nothing here that keeps the full price goes over 3 % unless it docks a column), and the icons-on-characters sheet says the lightest marks (numerals, pips, a halo, flat ground symbols) read at 40-60 px as well as full badges do. Whether the enamel itself is the problem is for Sky's eye: v17 (enamel, with d3's layout) is there to compare it against v18, v19, v20, v21 and v22, which swap only the language.

8 · How these were made

Codex image tool only (free; 5 kit sheets, see PROVENANCE.json with prompt, seconds and sha256 for each). The layouts, text and numbers are drawn in code over the real Handover plates (Latch). Kit sheets: k1 · k2 · k3 · k4 · k5. The solid-glyph hand is cut from the round 3 enamel icon sheets. Palette check, footprint method and the failed manila/peach tags are in PROVENANCE.json. People: none were prompted, so no era text applies; the cell are the same visitor capsules as round 3.
